claims.text: Nanocrystalline W38Ta36Cr15V11 undergoes radiation-induced precipitation at approximately 8 dpa and 1073 K.
W38Ta36Cr15V11 exhibits negligible irradiation hardening under the stated irradiation conditions.
Reducing the vanadium concentration from 11 at.% to about 5 at.% will suppress radiation-induced precipitation.
Compensatory adjustment of Ta and/or Cr can preserve BCC phase stability after reducing V to about 5 at.%.
Reducing V weakens negative high-temperature Ta-V and W-V chemical short-range order.
Vanadium content influences self-interstitial mobility and the balance between vacancy and interstitial motion in this alloy.
Reducing V will produce a closer balance between vacancy and interstitial mobilities.
Higher V content can accentuate segregation and precipitate formation through deleterious chemical ordering.
Reducing V will make the atomic distribution more homogeneous.
A more homogeneous atomic distribution will enhance recombination of radiation-induced defects.
Enhanced defect recombination will suppress the formation of large precipitates and voids.
The modified alloy will contain smaller and fewer irradiation-induced precipitates than unmodified W38Ta36Cr15V11 after approximately 8 dpa at 1073 K.
The modified alloy will retain a similarly negligible irradiation-induced hardness increase.
The modified alloy will have improved microstructural stability.
Reducing V to about 5 at.% will improve suitability for practical bulk fabrication.
The anticipated benefits apply up to roughly 8 dpa at about 1073 K.
Performance beyond approximately 8 dpa or at higher fusion-service temperatures is unverified.
